common_name: Fire Alarm Heuchera (Terra Nova Red Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Fire Alarm is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction bred for consistently bright red foliage color, which holds best with reliable moisture and some protection from the hottest afternoon sun.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Fire Alarm is a Terra Nova Nurseries coral bells selection prized for leathery leaves that emerge bright fire-engine red and deepen to a rich brown-red through summer before flaring back to vivid red in fall, giving the plant strong color interest across three seasons. Tiny cream flowers rise on wiry stems above the foliage in late spring but are secondary to the striking leaf color that is the main draw. Give it consistent moisture, especially if grown with any direct afternoon sun, since drought stress dulls the leaf color and can scorch the foliage. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor and share plants.

common_name: GRANDE Amethyst Heuchera (Oversized Purple Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to light shade; GRANDE Amethyst is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction bred for an unusually large, spreading clump, tolerating more sun than most coral bells in trials while still performing best with afternoon shade in a hot Gulf South summer.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to light shade, giving it plenty of room to spread; GRANDE Amethyst is bred to form a dramatically oversized clump compared to standard coral bells, reaching up to three feet wide, with rich violet-purple foliage marked by bold black-purple veining that makes a strong groundcover-scale statement in a shade bed. Because of its larger size it also tolerates a bit more sun than most Heuchera cultivars, though the deepest color and best performance still come with reliable moisture and protection from the harshest afternoon sun. Small sprays of pale flowers rise above the foliage in late spring but are secondary to the bold leaf color and scale. Divide only when necessary, since the plant's large-clump habit is part of its appeal.

common_name: Autumn Leaves Heuchera (Heat-Tolerant Color-Changing Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Autumn Leaves was bred by Terra Nova Nurseries from heat- and humidity-tolerant parentage (Heuchera villosa x americana), making it a stronger performer in hot, humid Gulf South summers than many coral bells cultivars.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Autumn Leaves is a coral bells cultivar bred from heat- and humidity-tolerant Heuchera villosa parentage, giving it noticeably better resilience through hot, muggy Southern summers than many of the more delicate purple-leaved cultivars. Its foliage shifts through the season, emerging warm red in spring, mellowing to taupe-bronze through summer, then flaring back to ruby-red in fall, giving it seasonal interest beyond a single static leaf color. Small cream flower spikes appear in late spring but are secondary to the changing foliage display. Give it consistent moisture through the hottest months and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to keep the planting vigorous.

common_name: Dolce Wildberry Heuchera (Compact Glossy Purple Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Dolce Wildberry is a Proven Winners introduction with a compact habit well suited to shaded containers, small borders, and edging.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Dolce Wildberry is a compact coral bells cultivar in the Proven Winners Dolce series, bearing glossy, scalloped purple leaves with dark charcoal veining on a tidy, dense mound that stays neat without sprawling. Its small size makes it especially useful for shaded container plantings, edging along a shade path, or tucking into a mixed bed where a larger Heuchera would overwhelm its neighbors. Small pale flower spikes rise above the foliage in late spring but are secondary to the rich, glossy leaf color. Provide consistent moisture and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.

common_name: Chocolate Covered Cherry Coleus (Seed-Grown Shade Coleus)

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; Chocolate Covered Cherry is a seed-grown coleus with rosy pink-and-mahogany foliage edged in crisp green, bred to hold its rich color well in shaded to partly shaded beds and containers.

directions: Plant in partial to full shade in moist, well-drained, fertile soil or container mix; Chocolate Covered Cherry is a seed-grown coleus bearing rosy pink and deep mahogany foliage with a crisp chartreuse-green margin, a rich color combination that reads well from a distance in a shaded bed or mixed container. It performs best out of direct, intense afternoon sun, holding its most saturated color in dappled or partial shade rather than full exposure. Pinch off flower spikes as they appear to keep the plant's energy directed into fuller, more colorful foliage rather than seed production. Pinch growing tips periodically through the season to encourage a dense, well-branched habit and prevent legginess.
